title: Living ashtpadi 16
tomorrow: Ashtpadi 17, salok: true in the beginning

cards: An apartment, the day before you move in. Not a cluttered room; a properly empty one. Bare floor, bare walls, a window.
What's in it? Nothing, you'd say. But that's not quite right.
The room is full of space. You can't see it, paint it or pick it up, and yet it's what makes the room any use.
You'll put a bed in it, a table, a life, and every one of those things will sit inside that invisible, shapeless room-ness.

teach.b: This week's salok said God has no form, no outline, no color, is beyond the three qualities, and is known by grace. Gurbani takes one more step. The One is nirankaar, formless: nir, without; aakaar, shape.

Sikhs use it as a name for God: Nirankaar. But Guru Arjan, elsewhere in the Guru Granth Sahib, pairs the two in one breath: formless, and Himself every form; without qualities, and with qualities, one.
Nirgun and sargun. Both, at once. It sounds like a riddle.
The empty room makes it less of one.
Space has no shape, and that's exactly why it can hold every shape. If space were square, round things wouldn't fit. Because it's nothing in particular, it can be around everything in particular.

Sikh teaching also says the One is sarab viaapak, pervading all: not sitting at the top of the sky, but in and through every thing, the way space is in and through every room. That's why the formlessness isn't cold.
Anything with a shape is over there, in one place and not another. The Formless has no edge to stop at.
So the One is also right here: in the kitchen, on the bus, in the hospital waiting room.
For someone living the sixteenth ashtpadi, the quiet corner, the bare wall, the space between the furniture aren't nothing. They make a fair picture of what has no picture.

how: Sikhs commonly call God Nirankaar, the Formless, and Gurbani describes the One as both nirgun and sargun, without and with qualities, pervading everything; gurdwaras keep no image of God.

o: a hymn sung without any music at all
the empty space inside a gurdwara hall
the Formless, a name for God with no shape

s: Gurbani says God is formless and also present in every form
nirgun and sargun, one: like space, shapeless and around every shape.
a formless God is far away, at the top of the sky
with no edge to stop at, the One is right here too.
nir, without; aakaar, shape: the Formless.

games.q: how can the One have no form and yet be in every form?
o: it can't; one of those is wrong.
like space: no shape of its own, so it holds every shape.
games.why: Gurbani pairs nirgun and sargun in one breath. space is nothing in particular, which is why it can be around everything.

practice: Let your eyes rest on a blank stretch of wall or floor, or on the air in the middle of the room, and look at the space between things rather than the things.
Notice that it's everywhere: around you, inside your cupped hands, between your breaths. If you pray, let Waheguru be the name of that everywhere.

wordCard.voice: Nirankaar, the Formless. No shape of its own, and so able to be in and through every shape, like space in an empty room.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: nirankaar, the Formless, from nir (without) and aakaar (shape).

carryVoice: Your line: formless, everywhere. No edge to stop at, so the One is right here too. See you tomorrow.
